summary.headline: Allied Digital Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 265 crore, but EBITDA margin held at 10% and PAT was Rs 13 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was Rs 265 crore, up 14% YoY, and H1 revenue reached Rs 526 crore (up 16%), the highest H1 in company history. EBITDA was Rs 27 crore at a 10% margin, marginally below Rs 28 crore in Q2 FY26, with management attributing margin pressure to talent and sales investments, competitive pricing and cost inflation. Services revenue grew 31% YoY and international revenue rose 36%, offsetting softness in domestic government projects. Trade receivables fell to Rs 264 crore and debtor days improved to about 84 from 96 at FY26 end, while the company stated it remains net cash positive.

segments.name: Services (managed services / annuity)
segments.commentary: Predictable multi-year annuity contracts grew 31% YoY in Q2 FY27. Management plans a greater contribution from managed services.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: International revenue rose 36% YoY in Q2 FY27, more than offsetting softness in domestic government projects. New US deal for infrastructure cloud and cybersecurity via offshore delivery centre.

segments.name: Government (domestic)
segments.commentary: Government share of revenue fell from 23% to 13% in Q2 FY27 per analyst. Management says the company is being selective due to hardware cost inflation; MIDC ILL win was the first government order after a gap of 3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management says it remains well positioned to sustain the Rs 1,000 crore annual revenue milestone, based on the H1 run rate.
Long-term ambition of 20% revenue CAGR; management says it has no fixed direct-vs-partner sales target and expects one of the three go-to-market buckets to drive the growth.
Priorities for rest of FY27: cost discipline, supporting growth investments and progressively strengthening profitability; no quantitative margin guidance given.
Management expects domestic government ordering to pick up, citing stabilising OEM pricing after mid-October 2026.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were disclosed on the call.
Noida Safe City bid submitted on 6 November 2026; results on other recently bid projects expected within 2 to 4 weeks.
Typical government build-and-maintain projects: 6-8 month implementation phase and 3-5 years of maintenance; revenue split about 60% build / 40% services.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of over Rs 74 crore in new orders and renewals in Q2 FY27; an analyst noted order book falling from Rs 120 crore to Rs 74 crore (management did not dispute the figures).
Large contracts are taking longer to close as clients scrutinise technology choices; small and mid-sized deals converting faster.
Hardware and OEM price spikes had made some government projects unviable; prices reported stabilising since mid-October 2026 and OEMs backing bids.
Management says product margins on MIDC ILL order are pre-blocked with the OEM. Government projects are seen as Rs 100-700 crore single tickets.
Management is seeking to shift toward direct enterprise customers, with partner-led and consortium deals currently providing scale.

qa_highlights.question: Order book has fallen from Rs 120 crore to Rs 74 crore; what is the status of the Noida Smart City project and government tender participation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had slowed government bidding due to price increases, but prices have stabilised since mid-October and OEMs are backing bids. Noida Safe City bid was submitted on 6 November 2026, with other bids pending results in 2-4 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: With government revenue down from 23% to 13% in Q2, how will the government vs enterprise mix evolve and how are contracts structured against payment and hardware inflation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MIDC pricing was locked with the OEM and billing is a 60:40 build-to-services split. Government payment delays occur but no large amounts are stuck; enterprise business is seen as more stable and longer-dated, with a stated focus on balancing the two.

qa_highlights.question: When will internal AI savings (32% L1 ticket deflation, 21% cost-to-serve reduction) outpace client-driven revenue deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figures and said AI-led ticket deflation is being run in parallel with existing staff before reducing people costs. Strategy covers automation, predictive AI support and agentic managed services.

qa_highlights.question: What is the target direct vs partner-led sales mix to achieve 20% CAGR over the next 24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no set direct/indirect target. Strategy has three buckets: partner-led large contracts, direct mid-size and small customers, and government large RFPs.

qa_highlights.question: Are there partnerships with large caps or acquisition plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited multiple OEM partnerships and said M&A is being explored, with no shortlist yet; focus areas are AI and cybersecurity.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: EBITDA margin flat at 10% and below prior-year Rs 28 crore EBITDA; investments in sales and talent are ongoing.
Revenue visibility: large deals are elongating, and government share has fallen to 13%; watch the Noida Safe City outcome and other bids in the next 2-4 weeks.
Hardware and OEM pricing volatility could again make government projects unviable.
Borrowings rose from Rs 98 crore to Rs 167 crore; watch working capital needs as project size grows.
AI-driven deflation in managed services pricing could reduce revenue before internal savings materialise.
Q2 order inflow of Rs 74 crore is modest relative to quarterly revenue of Rs 265 crore; watch order book trend next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and receivables, but cautious on margins and large-deal timing. Management repeatedly stressed selectivity on contracts and did not give quantitative margin or order-book targets. Some answers were evasive, notably on the AI savings question and the direct-vs-partner mix.
key_quotes: Customers are understandably cautious about committing to technologies that could quickly be superseded.
We have also adopted a disciplined approach to new business acquisitions, which clearly define profitability and commercial thresholds for evaluating prospective engagements.
So, I am happy that there are no sticky issues with our company in terms of corrections right now.
This marks an order win from a government agency after a gap of 3 quarters, validating our view that domestic government ordering activity is set to pick up again.
